checks: Verified original §§1, 3–4, equations (1), (3)–(5). Nonzero normals and positive full-dimensional fibers imply a continuous projection tail. Its compact Q-level gives both closed quantile criteria, including plateaus.

With b_base>Q, every nonnegative-drift base trace contributes more than Q at a·z+m(u), giving a uniform finite upper bound. With b_base≤Q, choose a minimum trace through z; Q<M ensures a nonempty complement and finite strict gap γ. Large tilted thresholds with gap kγ/2 capture exactly the selected full fibers and give arbitrarily large margins, including at equality.

At finite radius the maximizing sequence has bounded signed displacements. Clamping preserves mass Q and displacement, and its finite limit cap still has mass Q. Its left quantile is no larger than that threshold, so the new margin reaches the supremum. The same clamping attains the infimum for a fixed delta; finite and infinite domain branches then give both directions of the criterion.

At an interior sampled mark with strict atomic gap, the attained cap at nonnegative radius contains the mark and cannot capture the full own fiber. Thus it cuts properly. Raising the threshold by any positive amount removes positive own volume and does not increase other masses. A cap lighter than Q at the radius would have threshold strictly above its left quantile and violate maximality.
